entries.reason: the release carries no command event class at all: read with tools/mach32_methods.py from the 6.1.3 armv7 cache, none of its 236 classes in the MediaPlayer image at 0x31fe3000 has a name holding CommandEvent and none of its 41 categories adds one, with a nonsense selector absent as the control; and all 236 were read and none declares this member's selector. That is a per-class answer, which is what decides a member: the release's whole-cache selector list (selectors_armv7.txt, 113981 distinct names) has a line for repeatType, shuffleType and isNegative because other frameworks declare those names, which is the trap facts/MediaPlayer/MPMediaItem.md:105 records for albumTrackNumber. A class the release does not have is new code and cannot shadow anything, so there is nothing native for it to be. The command that produces it is already carried, and iOS 6's UIEventTypeRemoteControl has no shuffle-mode subtype, so the port's bridge never sends one and the command had no answer at all. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS ROW CLAIMED THE PORT'S BRIDGE BUILDS EVERY COMMAND EVENT LAZILY BY CLASS, so that carrying the event is what makes the command reach a handler. Nothing in this tree does that. APPLE PUBLISHES NO API THAT HANDS A COMMAND AN EVENT, so there is no delivery path to wire - on this release or any other. grep -rn 'deliverEvent|sendEvent' over MediaPlayer.framework/Headers reads NO file in SDK 26.2 and no file in 16.4, and MPRemoteCommand's public surface is exactly enabled, addTarget:action:, removeTarget:action:, removeTarget: and addTargetWithHandler:. An application sets a handler; only the system invokes it. 'deliverEvent:' is a PRIVATE selector on MPRemoteCommandCenter that no header declares, which is why the 6.1.3 selector universe's 113981 distinct names cannot hold it either - the 236 classes have no MPRemoteCommand to declare it - and why no file under packages/a/apple-backports/ defines it either, the name appearing only in this family's own prose about it. The port's own -charon_dispatch: (MPRemoteCommandCenter71.m:133) is reached from exactly one place, the subtype switch at :250-275, which maps ten UIEventSubtypeRemoteControl* cases; UIEvent.h in SDK 26.2 AND 16.4 declares exactly those ten, 100 through 109, with no shuffle-mode case at any availability, so no UIEvent on any iOS can carry one. MPChangeShuffleModeCommand's own row already says the honest thing - 'a real, stateful object; never messaged by this port's own bridge, since no old-style shuffle-mode gesture exists' - so this row now says the same about the event that command would have delivered THE LINE THAT PRODUCED THE FALSE CLAIM IS MPRemoteCommandCenter71.m:33, which says charon_command() "creates them lazily by class regardless of which object file defines them". That sentence is TRUE and it is about the COMMAND objects - MPRemoteCommand and its subclasses, which is what charon_command() allocates. Reading it as covering the events is what this row did; the next reader should not.
entries.effect: a real, addressable MPChangeShuffleModeCommandEvent a caller may construct, set -shuffleType on, and hand to its own handler; and never messaged by this port's own bridge, because no shuffle-mode gesture exists on this release to message it from - measured, and the same posture its repeat-mode neighbour's own row has carried since it landed
